system.description:
The Assamites have long claimed that Quietus arose for purposes beyond combat, and this power bears that out. By ritually bathing a willing subject in his own blood, an Assamite can purge that subject's mind of most supernatural influences. It sees frequent use on Assamites returning to Alamut after long sojourns in Europe or Taugast, to ensure they have not been turned against the clan. (Note: the source text's exact power level was lost to a printing/OCR defect; Storytellers should treat this as a high-level Quietus power pending further research.)

System: The character touches the subject and spends Blood Traits equal to the target's Willpower Trait total. The subject then contests a Willpower challenge once for each outside mental or emotional influence affecting him; success nullifies that influence. This power cannot remove influence carried by blood (including the blood oath) or purely mundane conditioning such as brainwashing, but it can strip away magical or thaumaturgical effects (such as a curse) provided the Assamite's own Quietus rating equals or exceeds the level at which the effect was cast.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Two: Saracens
